svg.text: Steering changes what the model writes
Descriptions written under steering are judged more positive or
negative, in line with the steering dose. See Figure 3, Panel A.
The words it writes then shift choice
Replaying the same text without steering still moves the later
choice in line with the dose. See Figure 3, Panel B.
Hidden states also shift choice beyond the words
Keeping the steered KV cache moves the choice further, well
outside eight random directions (grey). See Figure 3, Panel C.
Asked to repeat its descriptions word for word, its recall stays high
and broadly constant across steering doses. See Figure A6.
Effects persist when words are held fixed
Text written without steering, with valence injected only during
cache construction, still moves the choice across five models.
Only the valence direction has this effect
Other concept directions of equal strength do not consistently
Flipping the question flips the preference
With the question reversed, the same hidden state pushes choice
the other way. Lines are OLS fits. See Figure A5.
Preference training makes valence guide choice
In OLMo's checkpoints the effect is close to zero in the base
model and at full strength after DPO. See Figure 4.
The model removes a negative state but does
It removes negative steering at a dose-dependent rate, but seeks
positive steering no more than when unsteered. See Figure 5.
